items.stem: ISO/IEC 42001 is best described as a standard for:

options.text: Establishing and improving an AI management system within an organisation
options.rationale: Correct: ISO/IEC 42001 specifies a management system for AI, not a model-accuracy benchmark.

options.text: Measuring the accuracy of a specific machine-learning model
options.rationale: It is a management-system standard, not a model-accuracy metric.
It does not prescribe how to code models.
It certifies organisational management systems, not individuals.

items.explanation: ISO/IEC 42001 specifies an AI management system for an organisation.

items.stem: The main purpose of an internal audit in a management system is to:

options.text: Check whether the system conforms to requirements and is effective
options.rationale: Correct: internal audit verifies conformity and effectiveness before external certification.
Audit informs but does not replace management review.
Audit is not a disciplinary mechanism.
Audit is an assurance activity, not marketing.

items.explanation: Internal audit checks conformity and effectiveness.

items.stem: An organisation is planning its AIMS. Select TWO activities the standard's requirements expect during planning.

options.text: Assess risks arising from the organisation's AI systems
options.rationale: Correct: risk assessment is a core planning requirement.

options.text: Conduct an AI impact assessment considering affected parties
options.rationale: Correct: an AI impact assessment on affected parties is expected.

options.text: Publish the source code of every model externally
options.rationale: Public code release is not an AIMS planning requirement.
No standard can guarantee zero errors.

options.text: Outsource all AI decisions to a third party
options.rationale: Outsourcing decisions is not a planning requirement.

items.explanation: Risk assessment and an AI impact assessment are expected planning activities.
